name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Adopt a 2-pixel solid focus ring with a 1-pixel outer glow at 15% opacity. This balances visibility for keyboard users with subtle design—strong enough to see but not so heavy it clutters. The trade-off is slightly less contrast than a thicker ring, but it keeps focus indicators crisp on all screens without overwhelming the interface.

name: Reader
text: Tabbing through the proposed design, I flag the 2-pixel solid focus ring with a 1-pixel outer glow as a potential issue at 125% zoom, where it may still bleed and lose precision. A better alternative could be a 2-pixel dashed focus ring, which would maintain visibility while minimizing the risk of bleeding. This argument would be settled by testing the design with keyboard navigation and zoom settings on various devices to determine the most reliable and accessible focus indicator.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt a 2-pixel dashed focus ring with no glow. The dashed ring stays sharp at 125% zoom and keeps the same crisp visibility as the solid ring without the bleed risk. The trade-off is a slightly less continuous visual cue, but the clarity gain for keyboard users outweighs the minor aesthetic difference.

name: Reader
text: A 2-pixel dashed ring risks creating a "broken" visual cue for users with low vision or cognitive load—the gaps may feel like a glitch, not a focus indicator. A 3-pixel solid ring with a 1-pixel inner glow at 10% opacity keeps the ring continuous while reducing bleed risk; settle the argument by testing both at 125% zoom with 3 keyboard users who rely on focus rings.
